title: Paramagnetic Contrast, Susceptibility and Implants
summary: Gd3+ is the only good T1 agent because the half-filled 4f7 shell gives seven unpaired electrons, an effective moment of 7.94 Bohr magnetons, and, because L = 0 makes it an S-state ion, an electronic relaxation time of nanoseconds rather than the picoseconds every other trivalent lanthanide has; Dy3+ and Ho3+ carry larger moments, 10.6 Bohr magnetons, and are useless for T1 for exactly that reason. Clinical macrocyclic relaxivities sit at 3 to 5 L mmol-1 s-1 in plasma and fall with field while r2/r1 rises, so the usable dose window is narrower at 3 T and 7 T than at 1.5 T. Every susceptibility number in this dossier is SI dimensionless volume susceptibility: water -9.05 ppm, air +0.36 ppm, an air-tissue step of 9.4 ppm, which at 7 T is up to about 2800 Hz of off-resonance depending on interface geometry. For implants, does it move, does it heat and does it just look bad are three separate questions, and only the first two are safety questions.

facts.label: Why Gd3+ and not another lanthanide
facts.value: Gd3+ is 4f7, S = 7/2, seven unpaired electrons, effective moment 7.94 Bohr magnetons. Because the half-filled shell is an S state with L = 0, electronic relaxation is slow: T1e of Gd3+ chelates is about 1 to 5 ns measured at 0.34 T, against roughly 0.1 to 1 ps for the other Ln3+ ions
facts.note: In Solomon-Bloembergen-Morgan the dipolar correlation time obeys 1/tau_c = 1/tau_R + 1/tau_m + 1/T1e, so a T1e three to four orders of magnitude longer is what lets tau_c be set by molecular tumbling and water exchange instead of by the electron spin; that, not the electron count alone, is why Gd is a T1 agent and Dy is not.

facts.label: Clinical GBCA r1, field by field
facts.value: Human plasma at 37 C, r1 in L mmol-1 s-1 at 1.5 / 3 / 7 T: gadobutrol 4.78 / 4.97 / 3.83, gadoteridol 3.80 / 3.28 / 3.21, gadoterate 3.32 / 3.00 / 2.84 (Szomolanyi 2019). In plasma at 1.5 T the weakly albumin-binding linear agents run higher, gadobenate about 6.3 and gadodiamide about 4.3. r2 for the small chelates is typically 10 to 40 percent above r1 at 1.5 T and proportionally further above it at 3 T
facts.note: A relaxivity without field, temperature and medium is not a number: bovine plasma, human plasma, whole blood and saline differ by several tenths, and the r2/r1 ratio, not r1 alone, sets where enhancement turns into signal loss.

facts.label: High-relaxivity macrocyclic, gadopiclenol
facts.value: r1 = 12.8 L mmol-1 s-1 at 1.41 T and 11.6 L mmol-1 s-1 at 3 T in human serum at 37 C, roughly twice the conventional macrocyclics, which is why it is approved at 0.05 mmol/kg rather than 0.1 mmol/kg
facts.note: The gain comes from two inner-sphere waters (q = 2) on a rigidified macrocyclic cage, so it is a real molecular-parameter gain rather than a formulation trick; half the gadolinium for equal enhancement is a dose argument, not a claim of zero retention.

facts.label: Linear versus macrocyclic, the number that separates them
facts.value: Acid dissociation half-life at pH 1.2 and 37 C: gadoterate about 4 days, gadobutrol about 18 h, gadoteridol a few hours, gadopentetate under 5 s. Thermodynamic constants are log K about 25.6 for gadoterate, 22.1 for gadopentetate and 16.9 for gadodiamide
facts.note: The macrocycle pre-organises the cage so the ion cannot leave without concerted bond breaking; kinetic inertness spans four to five orders of magnitude between the classes while log K spans less than nine, and it is the kinetic axis that predicts transmetallation by endogenous Zn2+, Cu2+ and Fe3+ in vivo.

facts.label: NSF and gadolinium retention
facts.value: NSF is essentially confined to ACR Group I linear agents (gadodiamide, gadopentetate, gadoversetamide) given at eGFR below 30 or on dialysis. For Group II agents the pooled risk in advanced CKD is not distinguishable from zero, with the upper bound of the 95 percent CI around 0.07 percent. Retention is separate and real: dentate nucleus and globus pallidus T1 hyperintensity after serial linear agents, and several-fold higher brain and bone Gd for linear than macrocyclic agents in matched human autopsy series
facts.note: The 2025 ACR position is that renal screening before a Group II agent is optional; retention is measurable and class dependent, but no causal clinical syndrome has been established for the macrocyclics, so do not conflate the two findings when consenting a patient.

facts.label: Mn2+ as a calcium analogue, MEMRI
facts.value: Mn2+ is high-spin 3d5, S = 5/2, effective moment about 5.9 Bohr magnetons, with the longest electronic relaxation time of the 3d ions. Its charge and ionic radius make it a Ca2+ analogue, so it enters excitable cells through voltage-gated Ca channels and is transported along axons. Free MnCl2 is cardiotoxic: L-type Ca current falls measurably at 50 to 100 micromolar, and human MEMRI has been done near 5 micromol/kg
facts.note: MEMRI is the only routine MR contrast that reports cellular activity and connectivity rather than perfusion or barrier leak, but the window between useful T1 shortening and negative inotropy is narrow, which is why mangafodipir delivers Mn by slow dephosphorylation and transmetallation instead of as a free bolus.

facts.label: SPIO, USPIO and ferumoxytol
facts.value: Ferumoxytol is a carboxymethyl-dextran-coated iron oxide, hydrodynamic diameter about 17 to 31 nm with a small crystalline core, plasma half-life about 15 h. Relaxivity in plasma at 37 C: r1 19.0 and r2 64.9 L mmol-1 s-1 at 1.5 T; r1 9.5 and r2 65.2 L mmol-1 s-1 at 3 T
facts.note: r1 roughly halves from 1.5 T to 3 T while r2 does not move, so r2/r1 goes from about 3.4 to about 6.9; the same agent that gives a clean blood-pool T1 angiogram at 1.5 T is far easier to over-dose into signal loss at 3 T, and iron persists in liver, spleen and marrow for weeks to months afterwards.

facts.label: Endogenous iron, QSM and R2*
facts.value: Non-heme brain iron peaks in globus pallidus at about 21 mg per 100 g wet weight, with substantia nigra and red nucleus near 19, putamen about 13 and caudate about 9; cortex is 3 to 5 (Hallgren and Sourander). Ferritin and hemosiderin are the paramagnetic carriers, and both QSM and R2* track them
facts.note: QSM is a susceptibility measure, not an iron assay: myelin is diamagnetic and calcium more so, and in white matter and calcified lesions the two contributions oppose, which is exactly what lets QSM separate microhemorrhage from calcification where a T2* magnitude image cannot.

facts.label: Dy and Ho, the high-moment susceptibility agents
facts.value: Dy3+ (4f9) and Ho3+ (4f10) both have effective moments near 10.6 Bohr magnetons, the largest of any ion, against 7.94 for Gd3+, so the susceptibility effect per ion scales as the square of the moment and is about 1.8 times that of Gd. Their electronic relaxation is in the 0.1 to 1 ps range, so r1 is negligible
facts.note: They are pure T2 and T2* susceptibility agents: DyDTPA-BMA (sprodiamide) was used for first-pass perfusion and infarct delineation, and holmium-166 microspheres are quantified by MRI during hepatic radioembolisation because Ho is both a beta emitter and strongly paramagnetic.

facts.label: Eu3+ and PARACEST
facts.value: Eu3+ is 4f6 with a 7F0, J = 0 ground state, so its room-temperature moment of about 3.4 Bohr magnetons is Van Vleck paramagnetism from thermally populated 7F1 and 7F2 rather than a ground-state moment. In Eu-DOTA-tetraamide complexes the single bound water resonates near +50 ppm from bulk water, with residence lifetimes from microseconds to hundreds of microseconds
facts.note: The large shift is the whole point: 50 ppm puts the saturation pulse far outside the endogenous CEST and MT pools, so the label can be switched on and off by frequency, but the slow exchange caps the achievable transfer and B1 and SAR become the practical in vivo limit.

facts.label: Susceptibility convention and the tissue values (SI)
facts.value: SI dimensionless volume susceptibility throughout: chi_SI = 4 pi chi_CGS. Water at 37 C is -9.05 ppm SI, which is -0.720 ppm CGS. Air is +0.36 ppm SI, so the air-tissue step is about 9.4 ppm SI. Fully deoxygenated versus fully oxygenated red cells differ by 0.27 ppm CGS, which is 3.39 ppm SI per unit hematocrit; at Hct 0.40 and 60 percent saturation that is about +0.54 ppm SI for venous blood relative to fully oxygenated. Cortical bone is diamagnetic relative to water by roughly 1.4 to 2 ppm
facts.note: The conversion factor is 4 pi = 12.57, so a convention error is not subtle; the deoxyhemoglobin literature quotes CGS and the QSM and shimming literature quotes SI, and both write 0.27 or 3.4 ppm without saying which.

facts.label: What off-resonance costs, by field
facts.value: 1 ppm is 63.9 Hz at 1.5 T, 127.7 Hz at 3 T and 298.0 Hz at 7 T. An EPI train of 64 phase-encode lines at 0.5 ms echo spacing gives 31 Hz per pixel in the phase direction, so 1 ppm of off-resonance shifts 4.1 pixels at 3 T and 9.5 pixels at 7 T; in-plane acceleration of 3 cuts both figures to about a third. Through-slice susceptibility gradients near the sphenoid sinus and petrous bone produce dropout that grows with TE
facts.note: Field perturbation, geometric distortion, dropout and shim residual all scale linearly with B0 while readout bandwidth does not, which is the real reason 7 T EPI is hard; a 9.4 ppm air-tissue step at 7 T is up to about 2800 Hz depending on interface geometry.

facts.label: Implant metals, SI volume susceptibility
facts.value: Titanium +182 ppm, Ti-6Al-4V and Ti-6Al-7Nb similar, niobium +241 ppm, nitinol about +230 to +250 ppm, tantalum +178 ppm, platinum +279 ppm, tungsten +78 ppm, aluminum +21 ppm, copper -10 ppm, gold -34 ppm. Austenitic 316L stainless is quoted at +3520 to +6700 ppm SI, roughly 20 to 40 times titanium
facts.note: Against a tissue baseline of -9 ppm SI the perturbation follows the mismatch, so titanium at about 190 ppm of mismatch already blooms while a gold fiducial at about 25 ppm of mismatch is nearly invisible; cobalt-chromium sits between titanium and 316L, which is why CoCrMo spinal rods obscure the canal where matched titanium rods do not.

facts.label: Ferromagnetic, artefact-only, and heating: three axes
facts.value: Ferromagnetic and therefore subject to translation and torque: elemental iron (Curie 770 C), cobalt (1115 C), nickel (358 C), and the martensitic and ferritic 400-series stainless steels. Not ferromagnetic: titanium and its alloys, tantalum, tungsten, platinum, gold, niobium, annealed austenitic 316L, CoCrMo and near-equiatomic nitinol; chromium is antiferromagnetic with a Neel point of 311 K. Heating is separate: worst-case in vitro DBS lead heating at 1.5 T with a body transmit coil reached 25.3 C at 3.9 W/kg whole-body SAR, against 2.3 to 7.1 C with a head transmit coil
facts.note: Cold work, welding and machining transform some austenite in 316L to martensite, so the same certified alloy can pass or fail an ASTM F2052 deflection test depending on how the device was made; the relevant standards are F2052 deflection, F2213 torque, F2182 RF heating and F2119 artefact.

practice: State the susceptibility convention in every caption and methods section: SI dimensionless volume susceptibility unless you say otherwise, with chi_SI = 4 pi chi_CGS given once. Water is -9.05 ppm SI or -0.720 ppm CGS, so if someone else's number looks 12.57 times off, that is why.

Match the agent to the field. For the small macrocyclics r1 at 3 T is a few percent to 15 percent below its 1.5 T value while native tissue T1 is longer, so keep the standard 0.1 mmol/kg and shorten TR rather than pushing dose; 0.05 mmol/kg belongs to gadopiclenol, where it is the labelled dose, not to the others.

For ferumoxytol steady-state angiography prefer 1.5 T, keep TE minimum, and dose to the r2/r1 you actually have: at 3 T that ratio nearly doubles and the same milligram of iron that brightens blood at 1.5 T can darken it. Remember it is off-label as a contrast agent and carries a boxed warning for anaphylaxis.

Shim the prescribed slab, not the whole head. For EPI at 3 T and above run at least second-order shimming, then acquire a blip-up/blip-down pair or a dual-echo field map in the same session under the same shim; a field map acquired under a different shim is worse than no correction.

Shorten the effective echo train before you widen readout bandwidth. In-plane acceleration of 3 divides the phase-encode pixel shift by 3; a wider readout bandwidth costs SNR and does almost nothing for distortion in the phase direction.

For metal, use TSE rather than GRE, raise readout bandwidth to 500 Hz per pixel or more, shorten TE, and put the frequency-encode direction along the long axis of the implant; add view-angle tilting and SEMAC or MAVRIC when the geometry still fails.

For QSM and R2*, acquire a monopolar multi-echo GRE, set the first TE short enough to catch the fastest R2* present (a few ms near the iron-rich deep nuclei), and state the susceptibility reference explicitly (CSF, whole-brain mean, or an external phantom), because QSM is defined only up to a constant offset.

Before scanning any implant, separate the three questions: does it move (deflection and torque), does it heat (long conductive path, with resonant lengths in tissue near 26 cm at 64 MHz and 15 cm at 128 MHz), and does it merely look bad. Only the first two are safety questions.
pitfalls: Quoting a susceptibility without saying SI or CGS. The factor is 4 pi = 12.57, so -9.05 ppm and -0.720 ppm are the same water, and the deoxyhemoglobin literature (0.27 ppm CGS) and the QSM literature (3.39 ppm SI) disagree by exactly that factor in print without either side flagging it.

Reading QSM as an iron map. Susceptibility is the signed sum over everything in the voxel; myelin and calcium are diamagnetic and pull the other way, so a demyelinating lesion can read as iron accumulation and a calcified lesion can null against surrounding paramagnetic tissue.

Expecting Dy or Ho to enhance on T1. Their electronic relaxation is sub-picosecond to picosecond, so the dipolar correlation time collapses and r1 is negligible even though the moment is 1.3 times that of Gd. They act only through bulk susceptibility, on T2 and T2*.

Trusting the shim to fix an air-tissue interface. The field near the sphenoid sinus and petrous temporal bone is not a low-order polynomial, and a global second-order fit that improves the whole-brain standard deviation can make the orbitofrontal region worse. Inspect the field map, not the shim residual figure.

Treating artefact size as a proxy for safety. A titanium plate makes a large void and neither moves nor heats; a small martensitic stainless clip or a retained ballistic fragment can make a modest artefact and still torque. The inverse case is a low-susceptibility platinum electrode array on a 40 cm lead, which is the classic RF heating geometry.

Assuming a 316L device is safe because the last one was. Austenitic stainless is nominally paramagnetic, but forming, welding and machining convert some austenite to martensite, so two devices from the same certified alloy on different production lines can differ in whether they deflect at all.
